subject: Syncor Labs adapter errors — escalation and SLA alignment
messages:
From: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Syncor Labs Engineering <eng@syncorlabs.com>, James Patel <j.patel@consultica.io>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent adapter failures — urgent escalation

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing intermittent 502/timeout failures from the Redwood integration adapter this morning (around 07:45 PT). The failures affect webhooks for a subset of customer tenants — payloads are queued and replay attempts are failing with an upstream connection reset. We attached a clipped set of logs and a sample replay window for your team to look at (syncor_adapter_log_0328.zip, replay_window_sample.json).

Impact: ~8% webhook delivery failures for high-volume customers; some customers have opened support tickets. Our operations team has temporarily increased retry backoff which is causing delayed deliveries.

Can you escalate to infra and partner ops? We need:
- root cause triage and ETA for fix
- a temporary SLA/compensation discussion if deliveries continue to degrade
- an operations runbook for future incidents

We're available for a call today; prefer a 30-min slot between 10:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Evelyn Price
Head of Integrations | Syncor Labs
E: evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com
A: Attached: syncor_adapter_log_0328.zip (logs), replay_window_sample.json (sample payloads)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent adapter failures — urgent escalation

Thanks for the report and the logs, Evelyn — we’re on it. I created a support ticket (SUP-2389) and triaged with our on-call. Initial notes:
- Symptoms align with a transient connection-pool exhaustion in our adapter pool when Syncor sends backpressure bursts.
- I’ve attached the ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2389

Next steps I propose:
1) Immediate: 30-min debugging call (I can join at 10:30 PT). Ben, can you confirm infra availability?
2) Short term: a defensive hotfix to reduce outbound connection reuse + increase timeout on our side (target: rollout in 3–4 hours if validated)
3) SLA alignment: coordinate with you on a temporary playbook and an interim SLA for the impacted tenants while we stabilize.

Evelyn — please confirm 10:30 PT and share any customer IDs that should be prioritized. cc'ing Marissa to flag any commercial escalations if customers ask for credits.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent adapter failures — urgent escalation

On it — infra taking lead. Quick status:
- I’ve provisioned a debugging instance and started a packet-level trace against the failing tenants. Initial signal shows connection resets originating from a reused socket pool hitting abrupt closes at the partner endpoint.
- ETA for hotfix validation: 3 hours (will push staged rollout to 10% traffic first).

Jonas, can you accept the ticket and coordinate the runbook? We need: replay window, exact TTL and retention expectations, and a mutually agreed failure-handling flow (e.g., queuing policy, backoff, and prioritized replays). Evelyn, can your team provide the replay window retention guarantee and acceptable RTO for prioritized tenants?

Attachments: none (logs already in the SUP ticket).
— Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent adapter failures — urgent escalation

Thanks — I picked up SUP-2389 and ran a short impact analysis. Proposed technical guardrails while we investigate root cause:
- Temporary SLA proposal: 99.5% delivery for impacted tenants over a 7‑day rolling window while we deploy mitigations. If delivery < 99.5%, a one-time credit will be applied (details in attached draft).
- Suggested operational runbook steps (high level):
  1) Detect (monitoring alert triggers at 1% above baseline failure rate)
  2) Triage (run PREP script, collect stack traces, obtain replay window)
  3) Mitigate (apply connection pooling patch, increase timeouts, roll out to 10% -> 30% -> 100%)
  4) Postmortem and SLA reconciliation

I’ve attached a draft SLA and runbook (SLASyncor_draft_v1.pdf) — please review. Evelyn — to agree operationally we need a firm replay retention window (how long Syncor keeps raw payloads) and a point of contact for emergency replays. Can you confirm those and, if possible, provide a DocuSign point-of-contact for SLA sign-off?

On call availability: Jonas can do 10:30 PT and I propose we lock 30 minutes.

— Jonas
Director, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Syncor Labs Engineering <eng@syncorlabs.com>, James Patel <j.patel@consultica.io>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 13:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent adapter failures — urgent escalation

Appreciate the quick triage and the proposed runbook, Jonas. A few answers from our side:
- Replay retention: we retain raw payloads for 14 days by default; we can provide a prioritized 30-day retention for the impacted customers if needed (requires brief config change).
- Emergency replay POC: me (evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com) and our on-call engineer team at eng@syncorlabs.com.
- Legal/DocuSign: I’ll route the SLA draft to our legal; I can generate a DocuSign request once we finalize language.

I’m available for the 10:30 PT slot and we’ll be ready to share more logs during the call. For the call, can Redwood include a summary of the intended mitigation steps and a rollback plan?

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@syncorlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent adapter failures — escalation and SLA alignment (call scheduled)

Evelyn — thanks for the call today. Summary and next steps from Redwood:
- Hotfix: connection-pool reuse guard deployed to 10% at 11:15 PT; validation passed; full rollout completed by 12:40 PT. Monitoring shows delivery failures down to baseline.
- SLA: we agreed on the temporary SLA language (99.5% for 7-day rolling window) and Redwood will issue one-time credits if we miss the target. Draft attached (SLASyncor_draft_v1.pdf). Ben/Marissa to own the credit calculation and communication.
- Artifacts and ops: created shared Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-syncor-onboarding) and uploaded replay samples + postmortem checklist.
- DocuSign: Evelyn will generate the DocuSign request for the SLA once legal confirms language.

Action items:
- Ben: finalize credit calc and notify affected customers (ETA 48h).
- Jonas/Mateo: runbook PR and instrumentation improvements (ETA 5 business days).
- Syncor: confirm extended 30-day retention for prioritized tenants (Evelyn to confirm by EOD tomorrow).

Attachments: SLASyncor_draft_v1.pdf, replay_window_sample.json

Thanks all — closing the triage loop for now; will re-open SUP-2389 if anything regresses.

— Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142
